The worst case occurs when every person distributes their mass uniformly, i.e. each ball has mass \(1/66\).  
Then any choice of one ball per person gives each chosen ball a mass of \(1/66\).  
With 2025 people, at least \(\lceil 2025/66\rceil = 31\) people must pick the same colour (pigeon‑hole principle).  
Hence the sum of the chosen balls for that colour is at least  

\[
31 \times \frac{1}{66}= \frac{31}{66}.
\]

No smaller constant can work, because this situation forces a colour total of \(\frac{31}{66}\).  
Conversely, for any other distribution we can always assign each person to a colour where his ball’s mass is sufficiently small; the uniform case shows the bound \(\frac{31}{66}\) is attainable.  

Therefore the smallest constant that always suffices is  

\[
C = \frac{31}{66}.
\]

**ANSWER:** 31/66
